The budget summary is inside a floating `table` environment on the cover page. Floats can move off the cover page (or leave unexpected whitespace), which can break the required cover-sheet format. Prefer a non-floating `tabular` (or force non-floating placement) so the budget stays anchored on the cover page.

The inlined budget justification still mentions "simulation" as a student activity ("for simulation, 3D printing, and testing" on line 661). This is inconsistent with the experiment-driven pivot that removed simulation as a core activity throughout the rest of the proposal. It should be updated to something like "for design, 3D printing, and testing".

This latexdiff warning message about the missing `.bbl` file is being included as the first line of the generated `.tex` file. This will cause a LaTeX compilation error since it's not valid TeX. The warning should either be suppressed or the `.bbl` file should be generated before running `latexdiff` (by running `bibtex` on the original file first, as the message suggests).
```suggestion
% Bibliography file /home/runner/work/byu-mentored-research-tensegrity/byu-mentored-research-tensegrity/proposal-orig.bbl cannot be found. No flattening of \bibliography done. Run bibtex on old and new files first at /usr/bin/latexdiff line 2121.
```

`PLA–TPU` uses a Unicode en-dash character (U+2013). With `pdflatex` (per Makefile), this commonly triggers `Unicode character – not set up for use with LaTeX` and breaks the build. Prefer LaTeX-safe punctuation (e.g., `PLA--TPU` / `PLA\textendash{}TPU`) or add proper Unicode handling in the preamble if you intend to keep U+2013 throughout the document.
```suggestion
mechanical interlocking and prevent interface delamination. Because PLA--TPU interfaces are known to exhibit mixed-mode fracture behavior and potential void formation, print parameter validation and interface robustness will be explicitly evaluated during early testing.
```

LaTeX sentence spacing: `... optimization. Each student ...` will be treated as an abbreviation because the next word starts with a capital letter, so inter-sentence spacing will be too small. Use `optimization.\ Each ...` (or `optimization.\@ Each ...`) to force correct spacing after the period.
```suggestion
printing, mechanical testing, and data-driven optimization.\ Each student will be responsible for defining design variables, executing experimental or computational campaigns, analyzing data, presenting results, and drafting manuscript sections.
```

Consistency/typesetting: this paragraph uses `Year 2` while the rest of the document uses `Year~2` (non-breaking space). Also, `... project. Year~1 ...` will have incorrect sentence spacing in LaTeX because `Year` is capitalized; use `project.\ Year~1 ...` (or `\@`) to force end-of-sentence spacing.
```suggestion
design decisions, culminating in ownership of their research project.\ Year~1 focuses on technical skill acquisition and guided execution; Year~2 emphasizes independent hypothesis generation, experimental design, and peer mentoring. In
```

This sentence has a few clarity/grammar issues: (1) `approximately 100+` is internally inconsistent ("approximately" vs "+") and reads awkwardly; prefer "about 100" or "100 or more". (2) `contributed` is repeated, and `at UCUR and ASME IDETC` implies both venues; consider rephrasing (e.g., "at UCUR or ASME IDETC" and remove the duplicated verb).
```suggestion
participated in the design and testing of about 100 tensegrity
specimens, contributed to at least one \textbf{conference presentation} at UCUR
or ASME IDETC, and served as a co-author on a peer-reviewed manuscript
```

LaTeX sentence spacing + consistency: `... mentoring. Year 2 includes ...` will get incorrect spacing before `Year` because it's capitalized; use `mentoring.\ Year~2 ...` (or `\@`). Also consider `Year~2` for consistency with other sections.
```suggestion
\caption{Project timeline across two years (F = Fall, W = Winter, Su = Summer).  Summer terms support full-time research with intensive mentoring.\ Year~2 includes formal peer mentoring, where experienced students supervise newly recruited undergraduates.}
```

There are double spaces after periods here (e.g., after `loading.` and `simulation.`). This can lead to inconsistent spacing in the source and makes future diffs noisier; consider using single spaces consistently.
```suggestion
quasi-static compression and drop-weight impact loading. The key
contribution is a design--print--test workflow in which experimental
measurements are used directly to update a Gaussian-process surrogate
model, enabling sequential design selection without relying on
finite-element simulation. The surrogate is trained on peak transmitted
force, specific energy absorption (SEA), and compaction efficiency, and
a batch acquisition function recommends the next set of candidate
designs after each test round. The workflow combines automated model
updating and experiment selection with manual specimen handling and test
setup.

We define a parameterized family of unit cells using a core-wrapping
architecture in which rigid PLA struts are enclosed by continuous TPU
skins to improve interfacial interlocking. Design variables include
strut diameter and length, tension-element width and thickness, strut
count per unit cell, and tiling pattern. Specimens are fabricated on a
multi-material FDM system and tested under quasi-static compression and
instrumented drop-weight impact.

We will report how BO-selected designs evolve across iterations, how the
surrogate model changes as data accumulate, and what Pareto-efficient
trade-offs emerge between SEA and peak transmitted force within the
explored design space. We will also discuss practical lessons for
```

```suggestion
CIE-06: AI/ML: AI and ML for System Engineering,CIE,"This session invites papers on AI/ML approaches that advance the engineering, analysis, and design of complex systems characterized by extreme scale, intricate interactions, and pervasive uncertainties shaped by such as physical, human, and social behaviors, etc. While traditional AI/ML has succeeded in domains where problems are well-bounded, for example, single-task traffic flow prediction with structured and complete datasets, modern systems like power grids, manufacturing systems, and global supply chains present greater challenges. These include massive, heterogeneous, and incomplete data streams that require scalable frameworks; dynamic, multi-layered socio-technical interactions that call for methods such as graph learning, multi-agent models, and hybrid approaches; and deep uncertainties from incomplete knowledge, evolving dynamics, and unpredictable behaviors that demand principled techniques like Bayesian ML, conformal prediction, and physics-informed learning. This “Outputs (committed)” list omits `t3-prism.3mf`, but that file is present in `cad/t3-prism/`. Either document what the `.3mf` is/why it’s committed (and how it should be used), or remove it to keep the README in sync with the directory contents.
```

`generate_scaffold.py` imports `black` directly, but `bo/requirements.txt` doesn’t declare it. Even if it’s currently installed transitively, this makes the regen workflow fragile (a future dependency change could break `python bo/generate_scaffold.py`). Add an explicit `black` pin (or remove the `black` dependency by avoiding formatting in the generator).

When seeding existing data, the code ignores the `trial_index` returned by `ax_client.attach_trial(...)` and then calls `complete_trial(trial_index=i, ...)`. This assumes Ax trial indices will always equal the loop counter, which is not guaranteed and can lead to completing the wrong trial or raising if indices diverge. Capture and use the returned `trial_index` from `attach_trial` (as done in `tensegrity_campaign.py`).

`@pytest.mark.slow` is used but there’s no marker registration (no `pytest.ini`/`pyproject` marker config in the repo). This will emit `PytestUnknownMarkWarning` and can fail under stricter pytest settings. Either register the marker in a pytest config file or remove/replace it (e.g., with a plain comment or a built-in marker).
Minor doc typo: the sentence says “does not does not need to change.” Remove the duplicated “does not” to avoid confusion.

The module docstring says `SMOKE_TEST=true python bo/tensegrity_bo.py` produces a quick smoke run, but the generated `bo/tensegrity_bo.py` in this PR doesn’t read `SMOKE_TEST` (it always runs `range(21)`). The documented smoke workflow appears to be `python bo/generate_scaffold.py --smoke-test -o ...` instead—please update the docstring to match the actual behavior to avoid misleading users.

The comment says the reference skin cross-section `t*w = 4 mm^2` gives “~50% cushion”, but with `cushion = 1 / (1 + 0.6 * t*w / 4)` the value at `t*w=4` is 0.625 (~37.5% reduction). Either adjust the coefficient/reference so the stated 50% matches, or update the comment to reflect the actual scaling.

`run_tasks_until_done()` is assumed to return a non-empty list; indexing `responses[0]` will raise `IndexError` if the task fails/returns no responses. Add a guard (and ideally surface task status / error details) before dereferencing the first element.

If neither `EDISON_PLATFORM_API_KEY` nor `EDISON_API_KEY` is set, the script silently constructs `EdisonClient()` and will fail later with a less actionable error. Consider failing fast with a clear message telling the user which env vars are accepted (or require `--api-key`).

The references extraction only looks for structured fields named `references`/`bibliography`/`citations`. The committed JSON response for this task only contains `answer`/`formatted_answer`, so this will typically write the fallback message rather than a real extracted reference list. If you want reproducible `*-references.md`, parse the references section out of `t.formatted_answer` as a fallback (or persist a dedicated structured references field).

The main ranking table uses `||` at the start of each row (e.g., `|| Rank | Material | ...`). In GitHub-flavored Markdown this creates an extra empty column and often breaks alignment/rendering. Switch these rows to a single leading pipe (`| Rank | ...`) and keep column counts consistent.

The PLA–TPU interface evidence table is also written with `||` at row starts (and bold placeholders), which will render with an unintended empty first column. Update the table markup to standard `| ... |` rows so it renders correctly on GitHub.

This extracted references file contains two separate reference lists (a clean numbered list, then another "References" section with the PaperQA-style `(key pages x-y)` entries). If the intent is a concise list for BibTeX ingestion, consider removing the second, redundant section or clearly labeling why both are kept.

The manufacturing bullet says TPU 95A tendons, but later in this doc (and in the outreach script/trajectory) the project is described as using TPU 85A. Please make the tendon material/shores consistent throughout (and if both are used in different threads, explicitly scope which one applies to the manuscript vs. demos).

This file points readers to `manuscript/README.md` for venue rationale, but that path does not exist in the repo state for this PR. Consider either adding a link/reference to the PR/commit where the manuscript lives, or adjusting the pointer so the document is self-contained on the branch it lands on.

The Sources section lists several trajectory files (and `manuscript/references.bib`) that are not present in this PR’s repo state. For reproducibility, consider replacing these with links to the specific PRs/branches/commits where those artifacts live, or trimming the list to only files that exist on the target branch.

`outreach-topics-SUBMITTED.json` is written with a fixed filename, so rerunning the script will overwrite previous submissions and lose the earlier task_id(s). Consider including the task_id (or a timestamp) in the filename, or appending to a submission log, to preserve a history of runs.

The script prints the fetched task status but always returns 0 and writes artifacts even if the task is still running or failed. Consider gating artifact writing / exit code on `t.status` (e.g., nonzero on failure, or skipping the `.md` write until `success`) to avoid silently producing empty/partial outputs.

The script claims that a follow-up run can fetch a previously submitted task, but this path always creates a new Edison task before polling. If the first run times out and leaves `SUBMITTED.json`, rerunning will submit a duplicate LITERATURE_HIGH request and overwrite the saved task id instead of calling `get_task` on the existing id. Read `SUBMITTED.json` when present (or accept a task id argument) before falling back to `create_task`.

This only emits Markdown when `formatted_answer`/`answer` exists, but the committed result for this task says Edison returned structured artifacts rather than a `formatted_answer`. In that common case the script writes only the raw JSON and never produces the human-readable brief or `.references.bib` artifact described by the README/PR. Extract artifact messages and BibTeX from the verbose payload, or otherwise document that those files require a separate post-processing step.

The stroke rationale contradicts the stated specimen size: a 2.75 in / ~70 mm stroke is enough to compress a 25–50 mm cell well past the ≤30% first-test cap and likely to densification for many later runs. The load-cell range is still a valid reason to skip this frame for stiffness work, but the stroke claim should be removed or replaced with a specific fixture/clearance limitation if that is the real constraint.

Unused import: `os` is imported but not referenced anywhere in this module. Removing it avoids lint noise and keeps the generator minimal.

bo/requirements.txt is presented as the reproducible pinned environment for this scaffold, but it omits `pytest` even though the PR adds pytest-based smoke tests (and the PR description suggests running `pytest bo/tests`). In a fresh environment, `pip install -r bo/requirements.txt` won’t be sufficient to run the test suite. Consider adding `pytest` here or splitting runtime vs dev/test requirements and documenting the extra install step in bo/README.md.

> Multimaterial 3D printing of thick-panel origami
> PLA (Polylactic acid), TPU (Thermoplastic polyurethanes), ABS (Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene) and CFRP (Carbon fiber reinforced polymer) filaments for printing were used as received from Polymaker (China).
> 
> The thick-panel origami 3D model consists of two parts, one part is given TPU material, the other part is given PLA material, in which PLA part is completely wrapped and connected by TPU part, and the thickness for the wrapping and connecting is set to 0.4 mm (tTPU). The two 3D parts were designed and exported to STL files via Solidworks (V2016, Dassault Systèmes Simulia Corp., USA). After that, these two STL files were firstly assembled in Ultimaker Cura software and then were sliced with layer thickness set as 0.2 mm. The printing temperature for PLA material and TPU material was 210 °C and 220 °C, respectively. The bed temperature during the printing was set to be 60 °C. The printing speed for PLA material and TPU material were set to 60 mm·min−1 and 30 mm·min−1, respectively.
> 
> Uniaxial tensile experiments

> 
> Cyclic compression test
> Cyclic compression test of 3D printed a thick-panel Miura-origami sheet with 2 × 2 units was performed using an MTS machine (10 kN load cell, USA) at room temperature. The thickness of rigid panels and soft hinges were set to 2.2 mm and 0.4 mm. The loading and unloading speeds were both set to 10 mm·min−1. Detailed experiment process and result can be found in Supplementary Note [1](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37343-w#MOESM1).
> 
> Cyclic compression test of a 3D printed self-locking thick-panel origami structure was performed using an MTS machine (10 kN load cell, USA) at room temperature. The TPU thickness (tTPU), soft hinge length (2δ), unit wall width (b), and acute angle (γ) of 3D printed self-locking thick-panel origami structures mentioned in this test were 0.4 mm, 3.5 mm, 21.6 mm and 60.9°, respectively. The loading and unloading speeds were both set to 2 mm·min−1. Detailed experiment process and result can be found in Supplementary Note [6](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37343-w#MOESM1).
> 
> Quasi-static compression tests
> Uniaxial compression test of 3D printed self-locking thick-panel origami structures were performed using an MTS machine (10 kN load cell, USA) at room temperature with a crosshead speed of 2 mm·min−1.
> 
> Finite element analysis (FEA)
> To predict the deformation on the self-locking thick-panel origami unit, FEA simulations were conducted by using the commercially available software package ABAQUS (V6.14, Dassault Systèmes Simulia Corp., USA). We use the hyperelastic Mooney–Rivlin model with strain energy density function 
>  to describe the nonlinear material behavior of TPU. The material coefficients were set as C10 = 1.57 MPa, C01 = 2.18 MPa, which were obtained by fitting the uniaxial tensile experiments of TPU. The rigid panel formed by TPU wrapped PLA was simplified to a composite material and the modulus of the composite material was set to be 369.5 MPa by curve fitting based on experiment results. Tie constraints were used to connect the rigid panels to the soft hinges. Detailed FEA verification results were presented in Supplementary Note [12](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37343-w#MOESM1). The 3D model of self-locking thick-panel origami units (Structure I, Structure II, Structure III) were constructed and analyzed on ABAQUS/Explict (Simulia, Dassault Systemes). Solid tetrahedron quadratic element (element type C3D10M) was used to mesh the structures. The displacement was applied to the rigid plate above the self-locking thick-panel structure to simulate the quasi-static compression.
